AI.comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于将强化学习的先验知识与扩散模型相结合，有效解决了传统方法在复杂受限空间中精确动作建模的难题。通过RL先验引导扩散模型的训练和推理，DRIP在提升规划成功率、减少推理步骤和保持泛化能力方面展现出潜力，为自动泊车领域提供了一种新颖且高效的解决方案。

title: Unsupervised Deep Generative Models for Anomaly Detection in Neuroimaging: A Systematic Scoping Review
summary: Unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) based on deep generative modelling has been increasingly explored for identifying pathological brain abnormalities without requiring voxel-level annotations. By learning the distribution of healthy anatomy and generating pseudo-healthy reconstructions, these methods aim to localise deviations in a pathology-agnostic manner. Despite rapid methodological development - from autoencoders and variational autoencoders to generative adversarial networks and diffusion-based models - a structured synthesis of their application in structural neuroimaging is lacking. We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review of studies published between January 2018-December 2025 that applied unsupervised deep generative models to anomaly detection in brain MRI (and, less frequently, CT). Thirty-three studies met inclusion criteria. Methods were categorised by architectural family, and reported performance was synthesised across major pathology groups, with segmentation (Dice) and detection metrics (AUROC, AUPRC) disaggregated by evaluation level (voxel, slice, subject). For transparency, we also summarised dataset characteristics, dimensionality (2D vs. 3D), and thresholding strategies. Overall, unsupervised generative approaches demonstrate potential for pathology-agnostic anomaly localisation, particularly in settings where annotated data are scarce. However, methodological heterogeneity, limited external validation, and sensitivity to dataset characteristics remain important challenges. Emerging paradigms - including anatomy-aware modelling, diffusion-based frameworks, and alternative normative evaluation metrics - seek to address these limitations and improve robustness and clinical relevance.

AI.title_translation: 神经影像中异常检测的无监督深度生成模型：系统范围审查
AI.tldr: 该论文对神经影像中用于异常检测的无监督深度生成模型进行了系统范围审查，强调了其潜力和当前挑战。
AI.motivation: 尽管方法学发展迅速，但缺乏对无监督深度生成模型在结构神经影像中应用的结构化综合。
AI.method: 本研究进行了一项由PRISMA-ScR指导的范围审查，涵盖了2018年1月至2025年12月期间发表的将无监督深度生成模型应用于脑部MRI（以及较少见的CT）异常检测的研究。审查了33项符合纳入标准的研究，并按架构家族对方法进行分类。综合了主要病理组的报告性能，并按评估级别（体素、切片、受试者）分解了分割（Dice）和检测指标（AUROC、AUPRC）。同时总结了数据集特征、维度（2D vs 3D）和阈值策略。
AI.result: 三十三项研究符合纳入标准。无监督生成方法在病理无关的异常定位方面显示出潜力，特别是在带注释数据稀缺的环境中。
AI.conclusion: 方法学异质性、有限的外部验证以及对数据集特征的敏感性仍然是重要的挑战。新兴范式，包括解剖感知建模、基于扩散的框架和替代性规范评估指标，旨在解决这些局限性并提高鲁棒性和临床相关性。
AI.translation: 无监督异常检测（UAD）基于深度生成模型，在无需体素级注释的情况下识别病理性脑部异常方面得到了越来越多的探索。通过学习健康解剖的分布并生成伪健康重建，这些方法旨在以与病理无关的方式定位偏差。尽管方法学发展迅速——从自编码器和变分自编码器到生成对抗网络和基于扩散的模型——但它们在结构神经影像中应用的结构化综合仍然缺乏。我们对2018年1月至2025年12月期间发表的将无监督深度生成模型应用于脑部MRI（以及较少见的CT）异常检测的研究进行了PRISMA-ScR指导的范围审查。三十三项研究符合纳入标准。方法按架构家族进行分类，并在主要病理组中综合报告的性能，分割（Dice）和检测指标（AUROC、AUPRC）按评估级别（体素、切片、受试者）进行分解。为了提高透明度，我们还总结了数据集特征、维度（2D vs 3D）和阈值策略。总体而言，无监督生成方法在病理无关的异常定位方面显示出潜力，特别是在带注释数据稀缺的环境中。然而，方法学异质性、有限的外部验证以及对数据集特征的敏感性仍然是重要的挑战。新兴范式——包括解剖感知建模、基于扩散的框架和替代性规范评估指标——旨在解决这些局限性并提高鲁棒性和临床相关性。
AI.summary: 本文对神经影像中用于异常检测的无监督深度生成模型进行了系统范围审查。研究通过PRISMA-ScR指导的方法，综合了33项将这些模型应用于脑部MRI和CT的研究。结果表明，这些模型在病理无关的异常定位方面具有潜力，尤其是在注释数据稀缺的情况下。然而，审查也指出了当前方法的挑战，包括方法学异质性、外部验证的局限性以及对数据集特征的敏感性，并强调了新兴范式旨在解决这些问题。
AI.keywords: 无监督异常检测, 深度生成模型, 神经影像, 系统审查, 脑部MRI
AI.comments: 该论文的重要性在于其对神经影像领域无监督深度生成模型应用于异常检测的全面系统性审查。它不仅综合了现有技术和性能，还明确指出了当前方法的局限性和未来的发展方向，对于研究人员和临床医生了解该领域的现状和挑战具有重要指导意义。其创新之处在于提供了当前缺乏的结构化综合。

title: The PenduMAV: A Six-Input Omnidirectional MAV without Internal Forces - Design, Dynamics, and SE(3) Control
summary: We introduce the PenduMAV, an exactly actuated (6-input) omnidirectional multirotor that structurally eliminates internal forces at equilibria. The vehicle features one actively-tilting propeller and three propellers mounted on passive pendulum links via universal joints. This architecture achieves full 6D wrench generation while avoiding the structural and energetic costs of input redundancy and internal forces. After deriving the full multibody dynamics, we demonstrate that a forced equilibrium exists for every main platform pose. To asymptotically stabilize the closed-loop system, we design a coordinate-invariant nonlinear controller based on dynamic feedback linearization and backstepping, utilizing the left-trivialized error on SE(3). System stability is formally guaranteed through Lyapunov analysis of the zero dynamics. Finally, Gazebo simulations validate the approach, showcasing fully decoupled attitude and translational tracking under parametric uncertainty and actuator noise.

AI.title_translation: PenduMAV：一种无内力六输入全向MAV——设计、动力学和SE(3)控制
AI.tldr: PenduMAV是一种新型六输入全向多旋翼飞行器，通过独特的结构设计消除了平衡时的内力，实现了高效的6D力矩生成，并采用基于SE(3)的非线性控制器进行稳定控制。
AI.motivation: 旨在设计一种能够产生6D力矩的全向多旋翼飞行器，同时避免输入冗余和内力带来的结构及能量成本。
AI.method: 推导了完整的多元动力学模型，设计了一种基于动态反馈线性化和后退法的坐标不变量非线性控制器，利用SE(3)上的左平凡化误差来实现闭环系统的渐近稳定，并通过Lyapunov稳定性分析保证了零动力学的稳定性。
AI.result: 证明了对于每个主平台姿态都存在一个强制平衡点。仿真结果表明，该方法在参数不确定和执行器噪声存在的情况下，实现了姿态和翻译跟踪的完全解耦。
AI.conclusion: PenduMAV通过其创新的结构设计和先进的控制策略，成功实现了全向飞行和精确的6D力矩生成，同时避免了内力问题，并在仿真中验证了其稳定性和鲁棒性。
AI.translation: 我们介绍了PenduMAV，一种精确驱动（6输入）的全向多旋翼飞行器，它在结构上消除了平衡时的内力。该飞行器具有一个主动倾斜的螺旋桨和三个通过万向节安装在被动摆臂上的螺旋桨。这种架构在避免了输入冗余和内力的结构及能量成本的同时，实现了全6D力矩生成。在推导了完整的多元动力学之后，我们证明了对于每个主平台姿态都存在一个强制平衡点。为了渐近稳定闭环系统，我们设计了一种基于动态反馈线性化和后退法的坐标不变量非线性控制器，利用SE(3)上的左平凡化误差。通过对零动力学的Lyapunov分析，正式保证了系统的稳定性。最后，Gazebo仿真验证了该方法，展示了在参数不确定和执行器噪声下，姿态和翻译跟踪的完全解耦。
AI.summary: PenduMAV是一种新型的六输入全向多旋翼飞行器，其独特的设计（一个主动倾斜螺旋桨和三个通过万向节连接的被动摆臂螺旋桨）能够消除平衡时的内力，从而实现高效的6D力矩生成。文章详细阐述了其多元动力学模型，并提出了一种基于SE(3)坐标不变量的非线性控制器，利用动态反馈线性化和后退法实现闭环系统的渐近稳定。Lyapunov稳定性分析保证了系统的稳定性。仿真结果表明，该方法在参数不确定和执行器噪声下，能够实现姿态和翻译跟踪的完全解耦。
AI.keywords: 全向多旋翼飞行器, 内力消除, SE(3)控制, 动态反馈线性化, 坐标不变量控制器
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的多旋翼飞行器设计（PenduMAV），通过巧妙的机械结构消除了内力问题，这在传统的多旋翼飞行器设计中是一个挑战。SE(3)上的坐标不变量控制器的设计展示了先进的控制理论在解决复杂动力学问题上的应用。虽然仿真结果令人鼓舞，但未来的工作可以关注实际飞行测试以验证其鲁棒性和性能。

title: A Weak Penalty Neural ODE for Learning Chaotic Dynamics from Noisy Time Series
summary: The accurate forecasting of complex, high-dimensional dynamical systems from observational data is a fundamental task across numerous scientific and engineering disciplines. A significant challenge arises from noisy observations of deterministic dynamics, which severely degrade the performance of data-driven models. In chaotic dynamical systems, where small initial errors amplify exponentially, it is particularly difficult to develop a model from noisy data that achieves short-term accuracy while preserving long-term invariant properties. To overcome this, we consider the weak formulation as a complementary approach to the classical L2-loss function for training models of dynamical systems. We empirically verify that the weak formulation, with a proper choice of test function and integration domain, effectively filters noisy data. This insight explains why a weak form loss function is analogous to fitting a model to filtered data and provides a practical way to parameterize the weak form. Subsequently, we demonstrate how this approach overcomes the instability and inaccuracy of standard Neural ODE (NODE) in modeling chaotic systems. Through numerical examples, we show that our proposed training strategy, the Weak Penalty NODE, is computationally efficient, solver-agnostic, and yields accurate and robust forecasts across benchmark chaotic systems and a real-world climate dataset.

AI.title_translation: 弱罚神经网络常微分方程用于从噪声时间序列中学习混沌动力学
AI.tldr: 提出了一种弱罚神经网络常微分方程（Weak Penalty NODE）训练策略，通过弱形式损失函数有效过滤噪声数据，解决了从噪声数据中学习混沌动力学时标准NODE的不稳定性和不准确性，实现了对混沌系统和真实气候数据集的准确鲁棒预测。
AI.motivation: 从观测数据中准确预测复杂、高维动力系统（特别是混沌系统）是一个基本任务，但噪声观测严重降低了数据驱动模型的性能，使得从噪声数据中开发既能实现短期精度又能保留长期不变性质的模型变得特别困难。
AI.method: 提出了一种弱罚神经网络常微分方程（Weak Penalty NODE）训练策略。该方法将弱形式作为经典L2损失函数的补充，通过适当选择试函数和积分域，利用弱形式有效过滤噪声数据，从而克服了标准NODE在建模混沌系统时的不稳定性和不准确性。
AI.result: 经验证，弱形式能够有效过滤噪声数据，其损失函数类似于拟合过滤后的数据。该方法克服了标准NODE在建模混沌系统时的不稳定性和不准确性。数值示例表明，所提出的Weak Penalty NODE训练策略计算高效、与求解器无关，并在基准混沌系统和真实世界气候数据集中产生了准确且鲁棒的预测。
AI.conclusion: 弱罚神经网络常微分方程（Weak Penalty NODE）通过利用弱形式有效处理噪声数据，显著提高了从噪声时间序列中学习混沌动力学的准确性和鲁棒性，克服了标准NODE的局限性，提供了一种高效且实用的方法。
AI.translation: 从观测数据中准确预测复杂、高维动力系统是众多科学和工程领域的一项基本任务。确定性动力学的噪声观测带来了重大挑战，严重降低了数据驱动模型的性能。在混沌动力系统中，小的初始误差会呈指数级放大，因此从噪声数据中开发一个既能实现短期精度又能保留长期不变性质的模型特别困难。为了克服这一点，我们将弱形式视为经典L2损失函数的一种补充方法，用于训练动力系统模型。我们凭经验验证，弱形式通过适当选择试函数和积分域，能够有效过滤噪声数据。这一见解解释了为什么弱形式损失函数类似于拟合过滤后的数据，并提供了一种参数化弱形式的实用方法。随后，我们展示了该方法如何克服标准神经网络常微分方程（NODE）在建模混沌系统时的不稳定性和不准确性。通过数值示例，我们展示了我们提出的训练策略——弱罚神经网络常微分方程（Weak Penalty NODE）——计算高效、与求解器无关，并在基准混沌系统和真实世界气候数据集中产生了准确且鲁棒的预测。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种弱罚神经网络常微分方程（Weak Penalty NODE）训练策略，旨在解决从噪声时间序列中学习混沌动力学的挑战。该方法通过引入弱形式损失函数，并利用适当的试函数和积分域，有效过滤噪声数据，从而克服了标准神经网络常微分方程在建模混沌系统时表现出的不稳定性和不准确性。研究表明，Weak Penalty NODE计算高效、与求解器无关，并能在基准混沌系统和真实气候数据集中提供准确且鲁棒的预测。
AI.keywords: 混沌动力学, 噪声时间序列, 神经网络常微分方程, 弱形式, 数据过滤
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过引入弱形式损失函数来处理噪声数据，为神经网络常微分方程在混沌动力学建模中的应用提供了一个新颖且实用的解决方案。其创新点在于将弱形式的滤波特性与深度学习模型结合，有效提升了模型在噪声环境下的鲁棒性和准确性，对于需要从不完美数据中学习复杂动力系统的领域具有重要意义。

title: Symmetry-Breaking in Multi-Agent Navigation: Winding Number-Aware MPC with a Learned Topological Strategy
summary: In decentralized multi-agent navigation, agents that independently compute their controls without communicating goals or intentions can fall into symmetry-induced deadlocks because each agent must decide how to pass others. We study this problem under the assumption that each agent has access to the current observable states of other agents, including their positions, velocities, and radii, while their goals, intentions, and future trajectories remain unobserved. To address this problem, we propose WNumMPC, a hierarchical navigation method that quantifies cooperative symmetry-breaking strategies via a topological invariant, the winding number, and learns such strategies through reinforcement learning. The learning-based Planner outputs continuous-valued signed target winding numbers and dynamic importance weights to prioritize critical interactions in dense crossings. Then, the model-based Controller generates collision-free and efficient motions based on the strategy and weights provided by the Planner. Simulation and real-world robot experiments indicate that WNumMPC effectively avoids deadlocks and collisions and achieves better performance than the baselines, particularly in dense and symmetry-prone scenarios. These experiments also suggest that explicitly leveraging winding numbers yields robust sim-to-real transfer with minimal performance degradation. The code for the experiments is available at https://github.com/omron-sinicx/WNumMPC.

AI.title_translation: 多智能体导航中的对称性破缺：基于绕数感知MPC与学习拓扑策略
AI.tldr: 该研究提出WNumMPC，一种分层导航方法，通过强化学习学习绕数感知的拓扑策略，以解决多智能体导航中由对称性引起的僵局和碰撞，并在仿真和真实机器人实验中表现出优越性能和鲁棒的sim-to-real迁移。
AI.motivation: 在分散式多智能体导航中，由于智能体独立计算控制且不通信目标或意图，它们可能陷入由对称性引起的僵局，因为每个智能体都必须决定如何通过其他智能体。
AI.method: 该研究提出了WNumMPC，一种分层导航方法。它通过拓扑不变量（绕数）量化协作对称破缺策略，并通过强化学习学习这些策略。基于学习的规划器输出连续值的有符号目标绕数和动态重要性权重，以优先处理密集交叉中的关键交互。然后，基于模型的控制器根据规划器提供的策略和权重生成无碰撞且高效的运动。
AI.result: 仿真和真实世界机器人实验表明，WNumMPC能有效避免僵局和碰撞，并比基线方法表现出更好的性能，尤其是在密集和易发生对称性问题的场景中。实验还表明，明确利用绕数能实现鲁棒的sim-to-real迁移，性能下降最小。
AI.conclusion: WNumMPC通过利用绕数和学习拓扑策略，有效解决了多智能体导航中的对称性破缺问题，实现了高效、无碰撞的导航，并展示了强大的sim-to-real迁移能力。
AI.translation: 在分散式多智能体导航中，独立计算控制且不通信目标或意图的智能体可能陷入由对称性引起的僵局，因为每个智能体都必须决定如何通过其他智能体。我们研究了这一问题，假设每个智能体都能获取其他智能体的当前可观察状态，包括它们的位置、速度和半径，而它们的目标、意图和未来轨迹则无法观察。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了WNumMPC，一种分层导航方法，它通过拓扑不变量（绕数）量化协作对称破缺策略，并通过强化学习学习此类策略。基于学习的规划器输出连续值的有符号目标绕数和动态重要性权重，以优先处理密集交叉中的关键交互。然后，基于模型的控制器根据规划器提供的策略和权重生成无碰撞且高效的运动。仿真和真实世界机器人实验表明，WNumMPC能有效避免僵局和碰撞，并比基线方法表现出更好的性能，尤其是在密集和易发生对称性问题的场景中。这些实验还表明，明确利用绕数能实现鲁棒的sim-to-real迁移，性能下降最小。实验代码可在 https://github.com/omron-sinicx/WNumMPC 获取。
AI.summary: 该论文提出了WNumMPC，一种解决多智能体导航中对称性引起的僵局的分层方法。它利用绕数作为拓扑不变量来量化合作策略，并通过强化学习进行学习。WNumMPC包含一个学习型规划器，用于输出目标绕数和权重，以及一个模型控制器，用于生成无碰撞运动。实验结果表明，WNumMPC在避免僵局和碰撞方面优于基线，特别是在复杂场景中，并展示了鲁棒的sim-to-real迁移能力。
AI.keywords: 多智能体导航, 对称性破缺, 绕数, 模型预测控制, 强化学习
AI.comments: 该论文的创新点在于将拓扑不变量“绕数”引入到多智能体导航的对称性破缺问题中，并通过分层强化学习来学习和执行合作策略。这种方法不仅解决了传统方法在密集和对称性场景中容易出现的僵局问题，还通过明确利用绕数实现了鲁棒的sim-to-real迁移，这对于机器人领域的实际应用具有重要意义。

title: Future-Back Threat Modeling: A Foresight-Driven Security Framework
comments: Substantially revised framework and case study; clarifies FBTM as an assumption-centered, evidence-informed approach to decision-making under uncertainty, with explicit adversary/system contextualization and evidence-based analytical judgment
summary: Traditional threat modeling remains reactive-focused on known TTPs and past incident data, while threat prediction and forecasting frameworks are often disconnected from operational or architectural artifacts. This creates a fundamental weakness: the most serious cyber threats often do not arise from what is known, but from what is assumed, overlooked, or not yet conceived, and frequently originate from the future, such as artificial intelligence, information warfare, and supply chain attacks, where adversaries continuously develop new exploits that can bypass defenses built on current knowledge. To address this mental gap, this paper introduces the theory and methodology of Future-Back Threat Modeling (FBTM). This predictive approach begins with envisioned future threat states and works backward to identify assumptions, gaps, blind spots, and vulnerabilities in the current defense architecture, providing a clearer and more accurate view of impending threats so that we can anticipate their emergence and shape the future we want through actions taken now. The proposed methodology further aims to reveal known unknowns and unknown unknowns, including tactics, techniques, and procedures that are emerging, anticipated, and plausible. This enhances the predictability of adversary behavior, particularly under future uncertainty, helping security leaders make informed decisions today that shape more resilient security postures for the future.
comment: Substantially revised framework and case study; clarifies FBTM as an assumption-centered, evidence-informed approach to decision-making under uncertainty, with explicit adversary/system contextualization and evidence-based analytical judgment

AI.title_translation: 未来回溯威胁建模：一种前瞻驱动的安全框架
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种名为“未来回溯威胁建模”的前瞻性安全框架，通过从未来预期的威胁状态倒推，帮助企业识别当前防御中的盲点并提升未来网络安全韧性。
AI.motivation: 传统的威胁建模侧重于反应式，局限于已知的TTPs和历史事件数据，且威胁预测框架常与运营或架构脱节，无法有效应对由AI、信息战和供应链攻击等未来未知因素带来的严重网络威胁。
AI.method: 提出了未来回溯威胁建模（FBTM）理论与方法论，采用从设想的未来威胁状态开始向后推导的方式，识别当前防御架构中的假设、差距、盲点和漏洞。
AI.result: 该方法能够揭示“已知的未知”和“未知的未知”，包括新兴的、预期的和合理的战术、技术和程序，从而提高对抗未来不确定性时攻击者行为的可预测性。
AI.conclusion: 未来回溯威胁建模（FBTM）通过从未来预期的威胁状态倒推，能够有效弥补传统威胁建模的被动性和盲区，增强组织在面对未来高度不确定性时的安全韧性和决策能力。
AI.translation: 传统的威胁建模仍然侧重于反应式——聚焦于已知的战术、技术和程序（TTPs）以及过去的事件数据，而威胁预测和预测框架往往与运营或架构产物脱节。这造成了一个根本性的弱点：最严重的网络威胁往往不是来自已知的内容，而是来自被假设、忽视或尚未构想的内容，并且经常源于未来，例如人工智能、信息战和供应链攻击，在这些领域中，攻击者不断开发能够绕过建立在当前知识之上的防御的新漏洞。为了解决这种思维上的差距，本文引入了未来回溯威胁建模（FBTM）的理论和方法论。这种预测性方法从设想的未来威胁状态开始，向后推导以识别当前防御架构中的假设、差距、盲点和漏洞，从而对即将到来的威胁提供更清晰、更准确的视图，以便我们预测它们的出现，并通过现在采取的行动塑造我们想要的未来。所提出的方法进一步旨在揭示已知的未知和未知的未知，包括正在出现、预期和合理的战术、技术和程序。这增强了对抗行为的可预测性，特别是在未来的不确定性下，帮助安全领导者做出明智的决策，为未来塑造更具弹性的安全态势。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为“未来回溯威胁建模”（FBTM）的前瞻性安全框架，旨在解决传统威胁建模过于被动和局限于已知信息的缺陷。该方法通过从预期的未来威胁倒推，帮助安全领导者识别当前防御架构中的盲点和漏洞，从而制定能够塑造更强韧安全态势的决策。
AI.keywords: 威胁建模, 前瞻性安全, 预测性框架, 应对未来威胁, 攻击者行为预测
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种前瞻性的“未来回溯威胁建模”框架，创新性地将预测性思维引入传统被动的安全威胁建模中，有助于应对未来复杂多变的安全挑战，但其实际落地效果和操作性仍需在实践中进一步验证。

title: UrbanWorld2.0: A Multimodal Agentic Framework for Reality-Aligned 3D World Generation at City-Scale
comments: Accepted by ACM MM 2026, the code is available at: https://github.com/tsinghua-fib-lab/UrbanWorld2.0
summary: The automated generation of high-fidelity, city-scale 3D environments remains a formidable challenge with profound academic and industrial implications. However, existing methods struggle to achieve the necessary quality, fidelity, and scalability. To address this, we propose UrbanWorld2.0, a reality-aligned intelligent multimodal synthesis engine that creates detailed, city-scale 3D worlds of high fidelity. We introduce an agentic framework that leverages diverse multimodal foundation tools to acquire real-world knowledge, maintain robust intermediate representations, and construct complex 3D scenes. This agentic design, featuring dynamic data processing, iterative self-reflection and refinement, and the invocation of advanced multimodal tools, minimizes cumulative errors and enhances overall performance. Extensive quantitative experiments and qualitative analyzes validate the superior performance of UrbanWorld2.0 in real-world alignment, shape precision, texture fidelity, and aesthetics level, achieving a win rate of over 86\% against existing baselines for overall perceptual quality. This combination of 3D quality, reality alignment, scalability, and seamless compatibility with computer graphics pipelines makes UrbanWorld2.0 a promising foundation for applications in immersive media, embodied intelligence, and world models.
comment: Accepted by ACM MM 2026, the code is available at: https://github.com/tsinghua-fib-lab/UrbanWorld2.0

AI.title_translation: UrbanWorld2.0：用于城市尺度现实对齐三D世界生成的多模态智能体框架
AI.tldr: UrbanWorld2.0是一个基于多模态智能体框架的城市级高保真三D世界生成引擎，通过自反思机制和多模态工具调用实现了超越现有基线的高质量三D世界构建。
AI.motivation: 现有的三D环境自动生成方法在城市尺度上难以同时保证高质感、高保真度以及可扩展性，因此需要一种新的现实对齐智能综合引擎来解决累积误差等挑战。
AI.method: 提出了一种名为UrbanWorld2.0的现实对齐多模态综合引擎，引入了利用多样化多模态基础工具的智能体框架，具备动态数据处理、迭代自反思与精炼以及调用先进多模态工具的能力。
AI.result: 广泛的定量实验和定性分析表明，UrbanWorld2.0在现实对齐、形状精度、纹理保真度和美学水平上表现优异，整体感知质量的胜率超过86%。
AI.conclusion: UrbanWorld2.0成功实现了高保真、可扩展且与图形管线兼容的城市级三D世界生成，为沉浸式媒体和具身智能奠定了坚实基础。
AI.translation: 自动生成高保真、城市尺度的三D环境仍然是一项具有重大学术和工业意义的艰巨挑战。然而，现有方法难以达到必要的质量、保真度和可扩展性。为了解决这一问题，我们提出了UrbanWorld2.0，这是一个现实对齐的智能多模态综合引擎，可以创建高保真的详细城市级三D世界。我们引入了一个智能体框架，利用多样化的多模态基础工具来获取真实世界的知识，维护稳健的中间表示，并构建复杂的三D场景。这种智能体设计具有动态数据处理、迭代自反思与精炼以及调用高级多模态工具的特点，可最大限度地减少累积误差并增强整体性能。广泛的定量实验和定性分析验证了UrbanWorld2.0在现实对齐、形状精度、纹理保真度和美学水平方面的卓越性能，在整体感知质量方面对现有基线的胜率超过86%。三D质量、现实对齐、可扩展性以及与计算机图形管道的无缝兼容性的结合，使UrbanWorld2.0成为沉浸式媒体、具身智能和世界模型应用的前景广阔的基础。
AI.summary: 本文提出了UrbanWorld2.0，这是一个用于生成城市级现实对齐3D世界的多模态智能体框架，通过引入动态数据处理和迭代自反思等机制克服了现有方法的局限性，实现了卓越的3D世界生成质量与可扩展性。
AI.keywords: 城市级三D世界生成, 多模态智能体框架, 现实对齐, 高保真度, 计算机图形学管道
AI.comments: UrbanWorld2.0引入了智能体框架（Agentic framework）来处理城市尺度的三D世界生成，通过动态数据处理、自反思与精炼等机制有效减少了累积误差，具有极高的实用价值和学术意义。

title: Row-Stochastic Matrices Can Provably Outperform Doubly Stochastic Matrices in Decentralized Learning
summary: Decentralized learning often involves a weighted global loss with heterogeneous node weights $λ$. We revisit two natural strategies for incorporating these weights: (i) embedding them into the local losses to retain a uniform weight (and thus a doubly stochastic matrix), and (ii) keeping the original losses while employing a $λ$-induced row-stochastic matrix. Although prior work shows that both strategies target the same $λ$-weighted global loss, it remains unclear whether the Euclidean-space guarantees are tight and what fundamentally differentiates their behaviors. To clarify this, we develop a weighted Hilbert-space framework $L^2(λ;\mathbb{R}^d)$ and obtain convergence rates that are strictly tighter than those from standard Euclidean analysis. In this geometry, the row-stochastic matrix becomes \emph{self-adjoint} whereas the doubly stochastic one does not, creating additional \emph{penalty terms} that amplify consensus error, thereby slowing convergence. Consequently, the difference in convergence arises not only from spectral gaps but also from these penalty terms. We then derive sufficient conditions under which the row-stochastic design converges faster even with a smaller spectral gap. Finally, by using a Rayleigh-quotient and Loewner-order eigenvalue comparison, we further obtain topology conditions that guarantee this advantage and yield practical topology-design guidelines.

AI.title_translation: 行随机矩阵在去中心化学习中可以被证明优于双重随机矩阵
AI.tldr: 去中心化学习中，行随机矩阵因其自伴随性质和更小的收敛误差，在某些条件下可以优于双重随机矩阵。
AI.motivation: 去中心化学习中，如何有效利用节点异质权重是一个关键问题。虽然两种策略（嵌入权重或使用行随机矩阵）都旨在优化相同的加权全局损失，但它们在欧几里得空间中的收敛保证尚不明确，且行为差异不明。
AI.method: 提出了一种加权希尔伯特空间框架 L^2(λ;ℝ^d) 来分析两种策略的收敛性。在该框架下，分析了行随机矩阵的自伴随性质和双重随机矩阵的非自伴随性质，并推导了收敛速率。
AI.result: 在加权希尔伯特空间框架下，行随机矩阵表现为自伴随，而双重随机矩阵则不然。这导致双重随机矩阵产生放大了共识误差的惩罚项，从而减缓了收敛速度。因此，两种策略的收敛差异不仅源于谱隙，还源于这些惩罚项。研究推导了行随机设计即使在谱隙较小的情况下也能更快收敛的充分条件，并通过瑞利商和Loewner顺序特征值比较，获得了保证该优势的拓扑条件，并提供了实用的拓扑设计指南。
AI.conclusion: 在加权希尔伯特空间框架下，行随机矩阵比双重随机矩阵在去中心化学习中具有理论优势，尤其是在考虑了节点异质权重的情况下。这种优势源于行随机矩阵的自伴随性质，它避免了双重随机矩阵产生的惩罚项，从而实现了更快的收敛速度。
AI.translation: 去中心化学习通常涉及具有异质节点权重 λ 的加权全局损失。我们回顾了两种整合这些权重的自然策略：(i) 将它们嵌入局部损失以保持均匀权重（从而得到双重随机矩阵），以及 (ii) 保持原始损失，同时采用由 λ 诱导的行随机矩阵。尽管先前的工作表明这两种策略都以相同的 λ 加权全局损失为目标，但欧几里得空间的保证是否足够严格以及它们之间根本的区别仍然不清楚。为了阐明这一点，我们开发了一个加权希尔伯特空间框架 L^2(λ;ℝ^d)，并获得了严格优于标准欧几里得分析的收敛速率。在此几何结构中，行随机矩阵变为“自伴随”，而双重随机矩阵则不然，这产生了放大了共识误差，从而减缓了收敛速度的“惩罚项”。因此，收敛差异不仅源于谱隙，还源于这些惩罚项。然后，我们推导了行随机设计即使在谱隙较小的情况下也能更快收敛的充分条件。最后，通过使用瑞利商和 Loewner 顺序特征值比较，我们进一步获得了保证此优势的拓扑条件，并给出了实用的拓扑设计指南。
AI.summary: 本研究在加权希尔伯特空间框架下，分析了去中心化学习中两种处理节点异质权重的策略：使用行随机矩阵和双重随机矩阵。研究发现，行随机矩阵在该框架下具有自伴随性质，避免了因双重随机矩阵产生的惩罚项，从而在收敛速度上优于双重随机矩阵，即使其谱隙较小。研究还提供了保证此优势的拓扑条件和设计指南。
AI.keywords: 去中心化学习,行随机矩阵,双重随机矩阵,加权希尔伯特空间,收敛速率,异质权重,自伴随,惩罚项,拓扑设计,谱隙
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一个新颖的加权希尔伯特空间框架，为理解去中心化学习中不同权重矩阵策略的行为提供了深刻见解。其结论具有重要的理论和实践意义，尤其是在处理异质节点权重时。通过揭示行随机矩阵的优势，该研究为优化去中心化学习算法提供了新的方向。

title: Vision-Language Enhanced Foundation Model for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as an efficient paradigm for medical image segmentation, reducing the reliance on extensive expert annotations. Vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong generalization and few-shot capabilities across diverse visual domains. In this work, we integrate a VLM into a semi-supervised medical image segmentation model by adding a Vision-Language Enhanced Semi-supervised Segmentation Assistant (VESSA) that incorporates foundation-level visual-semantic understanding into SSL frameworks. Our approach consists of two stages. In Stage 1, the VLM-enhanced segmentation foundation model VESSA is trained as a reference-guided segmentation assistant using a template bank containing gold-standard exemplars, simulating learning from limited labeled data. Given an input-template pair, VESSA performs visual feature matching to extract representative semantic and spatial cues from exemplar segmentations, generating structured prompts for a Segment Anything Model (SAM)-inspired mask decoder to produce segmentation masks. In Stage 2, VESSA is integrated into an SSL framework as a plug-and-play teacher, providing template-guided pseudo-labels that complement the task-specific student model and strengthen supervision under scarce annotations. Extensive experiments across multiple segmentation datasets and domains show that VESSA-augmented SSL significantly enhances segmentation accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines under extremely limited annotation conditions.

AI.title_translation: 用于半监督医学图像分割的视觉-语言增强基础模型
AI.tldr: VESSA将视觉语言模型整合到半监督医学图像分割中，通过模板引导的伪标签显著提高分割精度。
AI.motivation: 减少医学图像分割对大量专家标注的依赖；半监督学习（SSL）虽高效，但在医学图像分割中仍面临挑战；视觉-语言模型（VLMs）在各种视觉领域展现出强大的泛化和少样本能力，为解决上述挑战提供了潜力。
AI.method:
本研究通过引入视觉-语言增强半监督分割助手（VESSA），将视觉-语言模型（VLM）整合到半监督医学图像分割模型中。该方法分为两个阶段：
1.  **第一阶段：** VESSA作为VLM增强的分割基础模型，通过包含金标准范例的模板库进行参考引导的分割助手训练，以模拟从有限标注数据中学习。给定输入-模板对，VESSA执行视觉特征匹配，从范例分割中提取代表性的语义和空间线索，为类Segment Anything Model (SAM) 的掩码解码器生成结构化提示，以生成分割掩码。
2.  **第二阶段：** VESSA作为即插即用的教师模型集成到半监督学习（SSL）框架中，提供模板引导的伪标签，以补充任务特定的学生模型，并在稀缺标注条件下加强监督。
AI.result: 在多个分割数据集和领域进行的广泛实验表明，VESSA增强的半监督学习显著提高了分割精度，在极度有限的标注条件下优于现有的最先进基线方法。
AI.conclusion: 本研究成功地将视觉-语言模型（VLM）集成到半监督医学图像分割框架中，通过提出的VESSA模型，有效解决了医学图像分割中专家标注稀缺的问题。VESSA通过两阶段的训练和应用，利用VLM的强大理解能力生成高质量的伪标签，显著提升了在有限标注条件下的分割性能。
AI.translation: 半监督学习（SSL）已成为医学图像分割的一种高效范式，减少了对大量专家标注的依赖。视觉-语言模型（VLMs）在各种视觉领域展现出强大的泛化和少样本能力。在这项工作中，我们通过添加一个视觉-语言增强半监督分割助手（VESSA），将VLM集成到半监督医学图像分割模型中，该助手将基础级别的视觉-语义理解融入到SSL框架中。我们的方法包括两个阶段。在第一阶段，VLM增强的分割基础模型VESSA被训练为参考引导的分割助手，使用包含金标准范例的模板库，模拟从有限标注数据中学习。给定输入-模板对，VESSA执行视觉特征匹配，从范例分割中提取代表性的语义和空间线索，为受Segment Anything Model (SAM) 启发的掩码解码器生成结构化提示，以生成分割掩码。在第二阶段，VESSA作为即插即用的教师模型集成到SSL框架中，提供模板引导的伪标签，补充任务特定的学生模型，并在稀缺标注条件下加强监督。在多个分割数据集和领域进行的广泛实验表明，VESSA增强的SSL显著提高了分割精度，在极度有限的标注条件下优于现有的最先进基线。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为VESSA的视觉-语言增强半监督分割助手，旨在解决医学图像分割中对大量专家标注的依赖问题。VESSA通过将视觉-语言模型（VLM）集成到半监督学习（SSL）框架中，利用VLM强大的视觉-语义理解能力。该方法分为两阶段：首先，VESSA作为参考引导的分割助手，利用包含金标准范例的模板库进行训练，生成结构化提示；其次，VESSA作为即插即用的教师模型，在SSL框架中提供模板引导的伪标签，以增强对学生模型的监督。实验证明，VESSA能够显著提高分割精度，并在极度有限的标注条件下超越现有最先进的方法。
AI.keywords: 半监督学习, 医学图像分割, 视觉-语言模型, 基础模型, SAM
AI.comments: 本论文的创新点在于将视觉-语言模型（VLM）与半监督学习（SSL）框架巧妙结合，提出VESSA模型，有效解决了医学图像分割领域数据标注稀缺的痛点。通过VESSA的两阶段设计，特别是利用VLM的泛化能力从金标准范例中提取语义和空间线索，并生成高质量的伪标签，为SSL框架提供了强大的补充。这种结合VLM作为“教师”指导学生模型的思路，在有限数据场景下具有重要的应用价值和广阔的研究前景。

title: Dripper: Token-Efficient Main HTML Extraction with a Lightweight LM
summary: High-quality main content extraction from web pages is a critical prerequisite for constructing large-scale training corpora. While traditional heuristic extractors are efficient, they lack the semantic reasoning required to handle the structural heterogeneity of the modern web. Conversely, well-pretrained generative Large Language Models (LLMs) offer superior document comprehension but are prohibited by excessive computational costs, limited context windows, and hallucination risks when applied at web scale. We present \textbf{Dripper}, a lightweight framework that resolves these bottlenecks through four contributions: (1) We reformulate extraction as a \textbf{constrained sequence labeling} task using SLMs (Small Language Models). This paradigm eliminates generative hallucinations and achieves exceptional efficiency, reaching a throughput of 3.08 pages per second on a single A100 GPU. (2) We construct \textbf{WebMainBench}, a rigorous benchmark of 7,809 human-annotated pages covering 5,434 unique domains and multiple languages. Evaluations show our Dripper-0.6B model \textbf{outperforms} heuristics like Trafilatura and rivals massive models like DeepSeek-V3.2(685B), GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro, offering an optimal efficiency-accuracy trade-off. (3) We demonstrate infrastructural value by \textbf{pre-training a 1B model} on a Dripper-curated corpus (63B tokens). This model significantly outperforms baselines in downstream tasks, proving the critical role of extraction quality and the effectiveness of our framework. (4) We \textbf{open-source} the Dripper-0.6B weights and codebase to facilitate the construction of high-quality datasets.

AI.title_translation: Dripper：使用轻量级语言模型进行高效令牌的主HTML提取
AI.tldr: Dripper是一个轻量级框架，通过将Web内容提取重新定义为受限序列标注任务，并使用小型语言模型，解决了大型语言模型在效率、成本和幻觉方面的瓶颈。它在WebMainBench基准测试中表现优异，超越了启发式方法并媲美大型LLM，同时开源了模型和代码。
AI.motivation: 从网页中高质量地提取主内容对于构建大规模训练语料库至关重要。传统的启发式提取器缺乏语义推理能力，而大型语言模型虽然理解能力强，但在网络规模应用时面临计算成本高、上下文窗口有限和幻觉风险等问题。
AI.method: Dripper框架通过四项贡献解决问题：1. 将提取任务重新定义为使用小型语言模型（SLM）的受限序列标注任务，以消除生成性幻觉并提高效率。2. 构建了WebMainBench，一个包含7,809个人工标注页面的严格基准测试。3. 使用Dripper-0.6B模型进行评估，该模型在效率-准确性权衡方面优于启发式方法，并与大型模型竞争。4. 通过在Dripper整理的语料库上预训练一个1B模型，证明了其基础设施价值，该模型在下游任务中表现优异。5. 开源了Dripper-0.6B模型权重和代码库。
AI.result: 1. Dripper框架通过受限序列标注实现了卓越的效率，在单个A100 GPU上吞吐量达到每秒3.08页。2. Dripper-0.6B模型在WebMainBench基准测试中表现出色，优于Trafilatura等启发式方法，并与DeepSeek-V3.2(685B)、GPT-5和Gemini-2.5-Pro等大型模型相媲美。3. 在Dripper整理的语料库（630亿令牌）上预训练的1B模型在下游任务中显著优于基线模型。
AI.conclusion: Dripper提供了一个高效、准确且可扩展的解决方案，用于从网页中提取高质量的主内容，通过利用小型语言模型和创新的任务重构，克服了传统方法和大型语言模型的局限性。其开源性质进一步促进了高质量数据集的构建。
AI.translation: 从网页中高质量地提取主内容是构建大规模训练语料库的关键前提。传统的启发式提取器虽然高效，但缺乏处理现代网络结构异构性所需的语义推理能力。相反，预训练良好的生成式大型语言模型（LLM）提供了卓越的文档理解能力，但在网络规模应用时，由于过高的计算成本、有限的上下文窗口和幻觉风险而受到限制。我们提出了Dripper，一个轻量级框架，通过四项贡献解决了这些瓶颈：(1) 我们使用小型语言模型（SLM）将提取重新定义为受限序列标注任务。这种范式消除了生成性幻觉并实现了卓越的效率，在单个A100 GPU上吞吐量达到每秒3.08页。(2) 我们构建了WebMainBench，一个包含7,809个人工标注页面（涵盖5,434个独特域名和多种语言）的严格基准测试。评估表明我们的Dripper-0.6B模型优于Trafilatura等启发式方法，并与DeepSeek-V3.2(685B)、GPT-5和Gemini-2.5-Pro等大型模型相媲美，提供了最佳的效率-准确性权衡。(3) 我们通过在Dripper整理的语料库（630亿令牌）上预训练一个1B模型，展示了其基础设施价值。该模型在下游任务中显著优于基线模型，证明了提取质量的关键作用和我们框架的有效性。(4) 我们开源了Dripper-0.6B的权重和代码库，以促进高质量数据集的构建。
AI.summary: Dripper是一个轻量级框架，旨在通过将网页主内容提取重新定义为使用小型语言模型（SLM）的受限序列标注任务，解决传统启发式提取器和大型语言模型（LLM）在效率、语义理解和成本方面的局限性。该框架引入了WebMainBench基准，并展示了Dripper-0.6B模型在效率和准确性方面优于启发式方法，并能与大型LLM竞争。此外，Dripper还证明了其在构建高质量训练语料库方面的价值，并开源了其模型和代码，以促进相关研究和应用。
AI.keywords: HTML提取, 小型语言模型, 序列标注, WebMainBench, 效率-准确性权衡

title: RetryGuard: Preventing Self-Inflicted and Attack-Driven Retry Storms in Cloud Applications
summary:
Modern cloud applications are built from independent microservices, offering scalability and usage-based billing. However, their reliance on independently-operating auto-scalers introduces coordination challenges. Default retry patterns can trigger "retry storms" during service miscoordination or adversarial overload, amplifying load, latency, and resource billing. These storms can cause either self-inflicted Denial-of-Wallet (DoW) or amplify the impact of DDoS attacks.
  To overcome these problems, we introduce RetryGuard, a distributed framework for productive control of retry patterns across interdependent microservices. By managing retry policy on a per-service basis and making parallel decisions, RetryGuard prevents retry storms, curbs resource contention, and mitigates escalating operational costs. RetryGuard makes its decisions based on an analytical model that captures the relationships among retries, throughput (rejections), delays, and costs. Simulations show that it outperforms established mechanisms, including exponential backoff, jitter, and retry budgets.
  Experimental results show that RetryGuard significantly reduces resource usage and costs compared to existing AWS policies, achieving more than 90% improvement in latency, and 98% reduction in storm size. We further demonstrate its effectiveness in a multi-layer Kubernetes deployment with the Istio service-mesh, where RetryGuard reduces the peak number of replicas by $3 \times$ and cumulative memory usage by 55%.

title: Bootstrap Dynamic-Aware 3D Visual Representation for Scalable Robot Learning
comments: Project Page: https://kolakivy.github.io/AFRO/, accepted by CVPR 2026
summary: Despite strong results on recognition and segmentation, current 3D visual pre-training methods often underperform on robotic manipulation. We attribute this gap to two factors: the lack of state-action-state dynamics modeling and the unnecessary redundancy of explicit geometric reconstruction. We introduce AFRO, a self-supervised framework that learns dynamics-aware 3D representations without action or reconstruction supervision. AFRO casts state prediction as a generative diffusion process and jointly models forward and inverse dynamics in a shared latent space to capture causal transition structure. To prevent feature leakage in action learning, we employ feature differencing and inverse-consistency supervision, improving the quality and stability of visual features. When combined with Diffusion Policy, AFRO substantially increases manipulation success rates across 16 simulated and 4 real-world tasks, outperforming existing pre-training approaches. The framework also scales favorably with data volume and task complexity. Qualitative visualizations indicate that AFRO learns semantically rich, discriminative features, offering an effective pre-training solution for 3D representation learning in robotics. Project page: https://kolakivy.github.io/AFRO/

title: Cooperative Safety Intelligence over V2X Networks: A Survey
comments: Published in IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials (Early Access). DOI: 10.1109/COMST.2026.3723946
summary: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) cooperation is reshaping traffic safety from an ego-centric sensing problem into a networked intelligence problem involving distributed sensing, cooperative perception, and coordinated decision-making. This survey reviews recent progress in V2X-enabled cooperative safety intelligence through a unified Sensor-Perception-Decision (SPD) framework, which characterizes how distributed observations are exchanged, fused, calibrated, and transformed into safety-ready evidence for risk-aware intervention. Within this framework, V2X networking conditions, multi-modal sensing, cooperative perception, and decision-making are analyzed as coupled components of a safety-intelligence pipeline. Cross-layer communication and networking constraints, including latency, synchronization, bandwidth, packet or feature loss, reliability, trust, and PQoS, are explicitly considered to assess whether shared evidence remains timely, robust, and actionable. Compared with prior V2X safety surveys, this work organizes the literature around a formal SPD safety loop and synthesizes representative methods, datasets, benchmarks, and platforms under communication-aware constraints from 2017 to 2026. It further examines semantic and task-oriented evidence exchange, bandwidth-efficient cooperative perception, ISAC-enabled V2X systems, safety-ready outputs, and evaluation practices under practical conditions such as delayed or lossy messages, pose misalignment, NLOS coverage, and heterogeneous deployment. The survey concludes with a roadmap toward scalable data infrastructure, PQoS-aware evaluation, embodied predictive intelligence, and trustworthy human-in-the-loop cooperation for next-generation V2X safety systems.

title: Audio Physical Dynamics Inspired Deepfake Detection for Voice Authentication Systems
summary: Voice authentication systems deployed at the network edge face dual threats: a) sophisticated deepfake synthesis attacks and b) control-plane poisoning in distributed federated learning protocols. We present a framework coupling audio physical dynamics deepfake detection with uncertainty-aware in edge learning. The framework fuses interpretable physics features modeling vocal tract dynamics with representations coming from a self-supervised learning module. The representations are then processed via a streamlined Multi-Layer Perceptron backbone, followed by a Bayesian ensemble providing uncertainty estimates. Incorporating audio physical characteristics evaluations and uncertainty estimates of audio samples allows our proposed framework to remain robust to advanced deepfake attacks, while our trust-based aggregation protocol secures the control plane against poisoning in network edge voice authentication systems.

AI.summary: 本文提出了一种受音频物理动力学启发的深度伪造检测框架，用于边缘语音认证系统。该方法融合了可解释的声道物理特征与自监督学习表示，并采用贝叶斯集成进行不确定性估计，同时利用信任基聚合协议防止联邦学习中的投毒攻击，从而在边缘环境中实现了安全稳健的语音认证。

AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将音频物理动力学特征与自监督学习相结合，应用于边缘网络语音认证，不仅增强了对深度伪造攻击的检测能力，还通过不确定性估计和信任聚合机制防范了联邦学习中的投毒攻击。具有很高的实际应用价值。

title: SparsePixels: Efficient Convolution for Sparse Data on FPGAs
summary: Inference of standard convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on FPGAs often incurs high latency and a long initiation interval due to the deep nested loops required to densely convolve every input pixel regardless of its feature value. However, input features can be spatially sparse in some image data, where semantic information may occupy only a small fraction of the pixels and most computation would be wasted on empty regions. In this work, we introduce SparsePixels, a framework that implements sparse convolution on FPGAs by selectively retaining and computing on a small subset of active input pixels while ignoring the rest, reducing the per-layer compute from $O(HWK^2C_{\text{in}}C_{\text{out}})$ to $O(n^2C_{\text{in}}C_{\text{out}})$ and the storage from $O(HWC)$ to $O(nC)$ when $n^2\ll HW$. Because computation always runs over a single pre-specified pixel budget that is frozen at synthesis, the inference latency is data-independent and constant at runtime. We show that, for identifying neutrino interactions in naturally sparse LArTPC images with 4k pixels, a standard CNN with a compact size of 4k parameters incurs an inference latency of 48.665 $μ$s on an FPGA, whereas a sparse CNN of the same base architecture, computing on less than 1% of the input pixels, achieves a $\times 73$ speedup to 0.665 $μ$s with resource utilization well within on-chip budgets, trading only a small percent-level performance loss. This work aims to benefit future algorithm development for efficient data readout in modern experiments with strict latency requirements of microseconds or below.

AI.title_translation: SparsePixels：面向FPGA稀疏数据的高效卷积
AI.tldr: 本文提出了SparsePixels框架，通过在FPGA上对稀疏图像数据进行选择性像素计算，实现了高达73倍的推理加速并保持了微秒级的极低延迟。
AI.motivation: 传统的标准卷积神经网络在FPGA上进行推理时，由于需要对每个输入像素进行密集卷积，导致深层嵌套循环产生高延迟和长的启动间隔；然而在许多图像数据中，输入特征具有空间稀疏性，大部分计算被浪费在空白区域。
AI.method: 引入SparsePixels框架，在FPGA上选择性地保留和计算一小部分活跃的输入像素而忽略其余像素，将计算复杂度从 $O(HWK^2C_{\text{in}}C_{\text{out}})$ 降低至 $O(n^2C_{\text{in}}C_{\text{out}})$，并通过在综合时冻结像素预算实现数据无关的恒定运行时延迟。
AI.result: 在LArTPC图像中识别中微子相互作用的任务中，稀疏CNN仅计算不到1%的输入像素，推理延迟从48.665微秒降低至0.665微秒，实现了73倍的加速，性能损失仅在百分之几以内，且资源利用率远在片上预算之内。
AI.conclusion: SparsePixels框架成功实现了在FPGA上对稀疏图像的高效卷积推理，在保持高吞吐和极低延迟的同时，将资源利用率控制在合理范围内，展现出在微秒级科学计算应用中的巨大潜力。
AI.translation: 在FPGA上推理标准卷积神经网络（CNN）时，由于需要对每个输入像素进行密集卷积（无论其特征值如何），深层嵌套循环往往会产生高延迟和长的启动间隔。然而，在某些图像数据中，输入特征在空间上是稀疏的，语义信息可能只占像素的一小部分，大部分计算都被浪费在空白区域。在这项工作中，我们介绍了SparsePixels，这是一个在FPGA上实现稀疏卷积的框架，它通过选择性地保留和计算一小部分活跃的输入像素而忽略其余像素，当 $n^2\ll HW$ 时，将每层的计算量从 $O(HWK^2C_{\text{in}}C_{\text{out}})$ 降低到 $O(n^2C_{\text{in}}C_{\text{out}})$，存储量从 $O(HWC)$ 降低到 $O(nC)$。由于计算始终在综合时冻结的单一预指定像素预算下运行，因此推理延迟与数据无关且在运行时保持恒定。我们表明，对于识别具有4k像素的自然稀疏LArTPC图像中的中微子相互作用，具有4k参数紧凑规模的标准CNN在FPGA上的推理延迟为48.665微秒，而相同基础架构的稀疏CNN计算不到1%的输入像素，实现了高达73倍的加速，延迟降至0.665微秒，资源利用率完全在片上预算之内，且仅带来百分之几的性能损失。这项工作旨在惠及未来现代实验中具有微秒级或以下严格延迟要求的有效数据读出算法开发。
AI.summary: SparsePixels是一个专门针对FPGA的稀疏卷积框架，旨在通过跳过空白区域、仅处理少量活跃输入像素来消除标准CNN中的冗余计算。该框架将计算与存储复杂度显著降低，实现了数据无关的恒定推理延迟，并在中微子相互作用识别任务中取得了73倍的加速效果。
AI.keywords: 稀疏卷积, FPGA, 卷积神经网络, 高效推理, 粒子物理
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种针对FPGA的稀疏卷积加速框架SparsePixels，通过选择性地保留和计算激活像素来减少计算量和存储需求，实现了数据无关的恒定推理延迟，在稀疏图像处理任务中取得了显著的加速效果。其创新点在于将稀疏计算与FPGA的高效流水线结合，非常适合具有微秒级延迟严苛要求的现代物理实验。

title: Good Locally Testable Codes with Small Alphabet and Small Query Size
comments: 24 pages. Changes from previous version: Corrected proof and statement of Thm.4.2. Comments are welcome
summary: Ben-Sasson, Goldreich and Sudan showed that a binary error correcting code admitting a $2$-query tester cannot be good, i.e., it cannot have both linear distance and constant rate. They also showed that there are no good codes if the alphabet is a finite field $\mathbb{F}$, the code is $\mathbb{F}$-linear, and the $2$-query tester is $\mathbb{F}$-linear. We show that those are essentially the only limitations on the existence of good locally testable codes (LTCs). That is, there are good $2$-query LTCs on any alphabet with more than $2$ letters, and good $3$-query LTCs with a binary alphabet. Similarly, there are good $3$-query $\mathbb{F}$-linear LTCs, and for every $\mathbb{F}$-vector space $V$ of dimension greater than $1$, there are good $2$-query LTCs with alphabet $V$ whose tester is $\mathbb{F}$-linear. This completely solves, for every $q\geq 2$ and alphabet (resp. $\mathbb{F}$-vector space) $Σ$, the question of whether there is a good $q$-query LTC (resp. $\mathbb{F}$-LTC) with alphabet $Σ$. Our proof builds on the recent good $2$-query $\mathbb{F}$-LTCs of the first author and Kaufman, by establishing a general method for reducing the alphabet size of a good low-query LTC.

title: Simulations between Strongly Sublinear MPC and Node-Capacitated Clique
summary: We study how the Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model in the strongly sublinear regime relates to the classic, graph-centric distributed models, focusing on the Node-Capacitated Clique (NCC), a bandwidth-parametrized generalization of the Congested Clique. In MPC, $M$ machines with per-machine memory $S$ hold a partition of the input graph. In NCC, we are given $n$ nodes that are themselves machines that know their full neighborhood but can send/receive only a bounded number of $C$ words per round. We are interested in the strongly sublinear regime where $S=n^δ$, for some constant $0 < δ<1$ and $C = MS/n$, where no simulation results are known. We explore when deterministic round-preserving simulations between these models are possible and when they are provably not, for different model parameters, problem families and graph classes. On the positive side, we provide techniques that allow, under certain restrictions, simulations with only constant overhead. On the negative side, we prove simulation impossibility results, which show that the limitations of our simulation results are inherent.

title: Cluster Aggregated GAN (CAG): A Cluster-Based Hybrid Model for Appliance Pattern Generation
summary: Synthetic appliance data are essential for developing non-intrusive load monitoring algorithms and enabling privacy preserving energy research, yet the scarcity of labeled datasets remains a significant barrier. Recent GAN-based methods have demonstrated the feasibility of synthesizing load patterns, but most existing approaches treat all devices uniformly within a single model, neglecting the behavioral differences between intermittent and continuous appliances and resulting in unstable training and limited output fidelity. To address these limitations, we propose the Cluster Aggregated GAN framework, a hybrid generative approach that routes each appliance to a specialized branch based on its behavioral characteristics. For intermittent appliances, a clustering module groups similar activation patterns and allocates dedicated generators for each cluster, ensuring that both common and rare operational modes receive adequate modeling capacity. Continuous appliances follow a separate branch that employs an LSTM-based generator to capture gradual temporal evolution while maintaining training stability through sequence compression. Extensive experiments on the UVIC smart plug dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms baseline methods across metrics measuring realism, diversity, and training stability, and that integrating clustering as an active generative component substantially improves both interpretability and scalability. These findings establish the proposed framework as an effective approach for synthetic load generation in non-intrusive load monitoring research.

title: How Do Large Language Models Learn Concepts During Continual Pre-Training?
summary: Human beings primarily understand the world through concepts (e.g., dog), abstract mental representations that structure perception, reasoning, and learning. However, how large language models (LLMs) acquire, retain, and forget such concepts during continual pretraining remains poorly understood. In this work, we study how individual concepts are acquired and forgotten, as well as how multiple concepts interact through interference and synergy. We link these behavioral dynamics to LLMs' internal concept circuits, computational subgraphs associated with specific concepts, and incorporate graph metrics to characterize circuit topology. Our analysis reveals: (1) LLMs concept circuits provide a non-trivial, consistent signal of concept learning and forgetting; (2) concept circuits exhibit a stage-wise temporal pattern during continual pretraining, with an early increase followed by gradual decrease and stabilization; (3) concepts with larger learning gains tend to exhibit greater forgetting under subsequent training; (4) semantically similar concepts induce stronger interference than weakly related ones; (5) conceptual knowledge differs in their transferability, with some significantly facilitating the learning of others. Together, our findings provide a circuit-level view of concept learning dynamics and motivate concept-aware training strategies, such as Circuit-aware Experience Replay, which uses circuit topology to prioritize concepts vulnerable to forgetting.

title: Measuring Narrative Polarization in Online Discourse
summary: Polarization research has demonstrated how people cluster in homogeneous groups with opposing opinions. However, this effect emerges not only through interaction between people, limiting communication between groups, but also between narratives, shaping opinions and partisan identities. Yet, how polarized information environments portray opposing interpretations of reality, and whether narratives move between content environments despite limited interactions, remains unexplored. To address this gap, we formalize the concept of narrative polarization and demonstrate its measurement in 212 YouTube videos and 90,029 comments on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Based on structural narrative theory and implemented through a large language model, we extract the narrative roles assigned to central actors in two partisan information environments. We find that while videos produce highly polarized narratives, comments exhibit significantly lower levels of narrative polarization, converging on shared core narrative structures. However, recurring narrative motifs capturing more complex actor constellations reveal additional differences between partisan environments.

title: Regenerating codes with minimal disk I/O cost achieving optimal tradeoff between storage and repair bandwidth
summary: Regenerating codes achieve the fundamental tradeoff between storage efficiency and repair bandwidth in distributed storage systems. Beyond these two parameters, disk I/O cost is an important measure of repair efficiency, capturing the number of stored packets accessed at the helper nodes during repair. A repair scheme is access-optimal if each helper reads exactly as many packets as it transmits, and is help-by-transfer if each helper sends stored packets directly to the newcomer without local computation. In this paper, we study functional repair of a single node failure in the regime where all surviving nodes participate as helpers. We introduce a framework based on signal flow graphs and gammoids, which separates the combinatorial structure of the repair process from its linear-algebraic realization. Within this framework, we construct functional-repair regenerating codes that attain every point on the optimal storage-bandwidth tradeoff curve. The proposed codes are help-by-transfer and access-optimal. Moreover, they operate over a fixed finite field and preserve the data-recovery property under an arbitrarily long sequence of repairs.

title: Cutting Corners on Uncertainty: Zonotope Abstractions for Stream-based Runtime Monitoring
summary:
Stream-based monitoring assesses the health of safety-critical systems by transforming input streams of sensor measurements into output streams that determine a verdict. These inputs are often treated as accurate representations of the physical state, although real sensors introduce calibration and measurement errors. Such errors propagate through the monitor's computations and can distort the final verdict. Affine arithmetic with symbolic slack variables can track these errors precisely, but independent measurement noise introduces a fresh slack variable upon each measurement event, causing the monitor's state representation to grow without bound over time. Therefore, any bounded-memory monitoring algorithm must unify slack variables at runtime in a way that generates a sound approximation.
  This paper introduces zonotopes as an abstract domain for online monitoring of general Robust-Lola (RLola) specifications. We demonstrate that zonotopes precisely capture uncertainty in the monitor's state and that their over-approximation produces a sound, bounded-memory monitor. We present a comparison of different zonotope over-approximation strategies for runtime monitoring, evaluating their performance and false-positive rates. Finally, we implement the most effective strategy in RLola and demonstrate improvements in both precision and runtime compared to existing approaches based on realistic benchmarks.

title: Counterexample Classification for Signal Temporal Logic Specifications
comments: The full version of the paper accepted by EMSOFT 2026
summary:
Signal Temporal Logic (STL) has been widely adopted as a specification language for specifying desirable behaviors of hybrid systems. One of the most common uses of STL is falsification, which attempts to generate counterexample signals that demonstrate how the system violates a given STL specification. A number of falsification methods and tools are available for efficient generation of counterexamples, which can be examined by the engineer to identify potential defects in the system. However, some of these counterexamples may be considered similar to each other in that they describe system behavior that stems from the same underlying causes or defects. Since examining counterexamples can be a labor-intensive task, a tool that presents a distinct set of counterexamples and avoids showing repetitive ones could reduce the amount of effort that the engineer spends in debugging.
  In this paper, we propose a counterexample classification method for STL specifications. Our approach is based on a novel criterion for classifying given counterexamples into a finite set of classes, each of which corresponds to a set of signals that share a common behavioral pattern. In particular, each class is represented by a formula in parametric signal temporal logic (PSTL), which provides a concise description of the signals in the class; then, the problem of checking whether a given signal belongs to a particular class can be formulated as finding parameter values for the corresponding PSTL such that the signal satisfies the formula. We propose an algorithm for automatically identifying classes from a given set of counterexamples and an efficient pruning method that leverages the concept of an inclusion relation between different classes. We demonstrate the efficiency of our algorithm and its utility on three hybrid systems, including automatic transmission, abstract fuel control, and robot navigation.

title: The $\mathbf{P}$-Completeness of Inverted Index Traversal: On the Complexity of Evaluating Boolean Query DAGs
summary:
Modern AI agents increasingly rely on search infrastructure to execute complex, neuro-symbolic reasoning workflows. These workflows often compile into deeply nested, non-monotonic Boolean queries over text fields. However, standard query evaluation strategies over inverted indices face severe theoretical limits when handling these structures. Stateful iterator models (Document-at-a-Time) are structurally bounded by $\text{NC}^1$ formula evaluation, suffering a worst-case $O(2^{|Q|})$ exponential blowup in query complexity when unrolling re-convergent logic. Conversely, recursive materialization models (Term-at-a-Time) incur an $Ω(|U|)$ space complexity penalty (the Universal Scan) when evaluating logical negation over the document universe.
  In this paper, we establish the theoretical boundaries of executing complex logic natively over an inverted index. We formalize a retrieval language ($\mathcal{L}_R$) based on Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) and prove that its evaluation problem is strictly \textbf{$\mathbf{P}$-Complete}. To make evaluation tractable, we introduce \texttt{ComputePN}, a deterministic, sparsity-aware evaluation algorithm. By decoupling logical negation from universe-scale materialization via a novel Positive-Negative dual representation, and utilizing native DAG memoization, \texttt{ComputePN} strictly bounds evaluation time to $O(|Q| \cdot |U_{\mathit{active}}|)$. This approach successfully evaluates $\mathbf{P}$-Complete queries natively over the index, avoiding both the combinatorial tree-expansion bottleneck and the universal scan penalty, laying the formal foundation for computational retrieval.

title: Language Family Matters: Evaluating LLM-Based ASR Across Linguistic Boundaries
summary: Large Language Model (LLM)-powered Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems achieve strong performance with limited resources by linking a frozen speech encoder to a pretrained LLM via a lightweight connector. Prior work trains a separate connector per language, overlooking linguistic relatedness. We propose an efficient and novel connector-sharing strategy based on linguistic family membership, enabling one connector per family, and empirically validate its effectiveness across two multilingual LLMs and two real-world corpora spanning curated and crowd-sourced speech. Our results show that family-based connectors reduce parameter count while improving generalization across domains, offering a practical and scalable strategy for multilingual ASR deployment.

title: Parametric and Generative Forecasts of EPEX Day-Ahead Energy Market Curves
summary:
We propose two methodologies for modelling aggregated supply and demand curves in the EPEX SPOT Day-Ahead market, emphasizing generative models as a way to recover distributional variability. The first is a low-dimensional parametric representation that yields deterministic point forecasts; the second is a high-dimensional order-level representation that samples from a conditional distribution of plausible curves. Both model the full curve structure, enabling the analysis of price sensitivity, volume sensitivity, and price impact.
  The parametric representation uses plateau levels, elastic-region boundaries, and polynomial coefficients, forecast with eXtreme Gradient Boosting. The main contribution is the generative representation, which uses price arrivals and volume-increment marks and is implemented with conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models.
  Using French EPEX data from 2021 to 2024, we evaluate both approaches through curve reconstruction and a price-maker storage optimization problem. The parametric implementation provides a deterministic reference, while the diffusion-based implementation produces distributions of plausible curves and achieves higher realized profits and smaller gaps to an oracle benchmark in the storage application.

title: The Impact of Shared Autonomous Vehicles in Microtransit Systems: A Case Study in Atlanta
summary: Microtransit systems represent an enhancement to solve the first- and last-mile problem, integrating traditional rail and bus networks with on-demand shuttles into a flexible, integrated system. This type of demand responsive transport provides greater accessibility and higher quality levels of service compared to conventional fixed-route transit services. Advances in technology offer further opportunities to enhance microtransit performance. In particular, shared autonomous vehicles (SAVs) have the potential to transform the mobility landscape by enabling more sustainable operations, enhanced user convenience, and greater system reliability. This paper investigates the integration of SAVs in microtransit systems, advancing the technological capabilities of on-demand shuttles. A shuttle dispatching optimization model is enhanced to accommodate for driver behavior and SAV functionalities. A model predictive control approach is proposed that dynamically rebalances on-demand shuttles towards areas of higher demand without relying on vast historical data. Scenario-driven experiments are conducted using data from the MARTA Reach microtransit pilot. The results demonstrate that SAVs can elevate both service quality and user experience compared to traditional on-demand shuttles in microtransit systems.

title: WorldBench: Benchmarking Physical Understanding of World Models by Isolating Physics Concepts
summary: Recent advances in generative foundational models, often termed "world models," have propelled interest in applying them to critical tasks like robotic planning and autonomous system training. For reliable deployment, these models must exhibit high physical fidelity, accurately simulating real-world dynamics. Existing physics-based video benchmarks, however, suffer from entanglement, where a single test simultaneously evaluates multiple physical laws and concepts, fundamentally limiting their diagnostic capability. We introduce WorldBench, a novel video-based benchmark specifically designed for concept-specific, disentangled evaluation, allowing us to rigorously isolate and assess understanding of a single physical concept or law at a time. To make WorldBench comprehensive, we design benchmarks at two different levels: 1) an evaluation of intuitive physical understanding with higher level concepts such as object permanence or scale/perspective, and 2) an evaluation of low-level physical constants and material properties such as friction coefficients or fluid viscosity, allowing to measure excatly how far from reality generated videos are. When SOTA video-based world models are evaluated on WorldBench, we find specific patterns of failure in particular physics concepts, with all tested models lacking the physical consistency required to generate reliable real-world interactions. Through its concept-specific evaluation, WorldBench offers a more nuanced and scalable framework for rigorously evaluating the physical reasoning capabilities of video generation and world models, paving the way for more robust and generalizable world-model-driven learning.

title: Large Language Models: A Mathematical Formulation
summary: Large language models (LLMs) process and predict sequences containing text to answer questions, and address tasks including document summarization, providing recommendations, writing software and solving quantitative problems. We provide a mathematical framework for LLMs by describing the encoding of text sequences into sequences of tokens, defining the architecture for next-token prediction models, explaining how these models are learned from data, and demonstrating how they are deployed to address a variety of tasks. The mathematical sophistication required to understand this material is not high, and relies on straightforward ideas from information theory, probability and optimization. Nonetheless, the combination of ideas resting on these different components from the mathematical sciences yields a complex algorithmic structure; and this algorithmic structure has demonstrated remarkable empirical successes. The mathematical framework established here provides a platform from which it is possible to formulate and address questions concerning the accuracy, efficiency and robustness of the algorithms that constitute LLMs. The framework also suggests directions for development of modified and new methodologies.

title: KAN We Flow? Advancing Robotic Manipulation with 3D Flow Matching via KAN & RWKV
summary: Diffusion-based visuomotor policies excel at modeling action distributions but are inference-inefficient, since recursively denoising from noise to policy requires many steps and heavy UNet backbones, which hinders deployment on resource-constrained robots. Flow matching alleviates the sampling burden by learning a one-step vector field, yet prior implementations still inherit large UNet-style architectures. In this work, we present KAN-We-Flow, a flow-matching policy that draws on recent advances in Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) from vision to build a lightweight and highly expressive backbone for 3D manipulation. Concretely, we introduce an RWKV-KAN block: an RWKV first performs efficient time/channel mixing to propagate task context, and a subsequent GroupKAN layer applies learnable spline-based, groupwise functional mappings to perform feature-wise nonlinear calibration of the action mapping on RWKV outputs. Moreover, we introduce an Action Consistency Regularization (ACR), a lightweight auxiliary loss that enforces alignment between predicted action trajectories and expert demonstrations via Euler extrapolation, providing additional supervision to stabilize training and improve policy precision. Without resorting to large UNets, our design reduces parameters by 86.8\%, maintains fast runtime, and achieves state-of-the-art success rates on Adroit, Meta-World, and DexArt benchmarks. Our project page can be viewed in \href{https://zhihaochen-2003.github.io/KAN-We-Flow.github.io/}{\textcolor{red}{link}}

title: How (Not) to Hybridize Neural and Mechanistic Models for Epidemiological Forecasting
summary: Epidemiological forecasting from surveillance data is a hard problem and hybridizing mechanistic compartmental models with neural models is a natural direction. The mechanistic structure helps keep trajectories epidemiologically plausible, while neural components can capture non-stationary, data-adaptive effects. In practice, however, many seemingly straightforward couplings fail under partial observability and continually shifting transmission dynamics driven by behavior, waning immunity, seasonality, and interventions. We catalog these failure modes and show that robust performance requires making non-stationarity explicit: we extract multi-scale structure from the observed infection series and use it as an interpretable control signal for a controlled neural ODE coupled to an epidemiological model. Concretely, we decompose infections into trend, seasonal, and residual components and use these signals to drive continuous-time latent dynamics while jointly forecasting and inferring time-varying transmission, recovery, and immunity-loss rates. Across early outbreak and multi-wave regimes, our approach attains the lowest RMSE on five datasets (21-63% reduction over the strongest default-configured baseline), achieves the best peak detection accuracy, and infers time-varying epidemiological rates within ground-truth ranges, without relying on auxiliary covariates.

title: Community Concealment from Graph Neural Networks
summary: Graph neural networks (GNNs) enable powerful unsupervised learning of communities. However, such inference may inadvertently expose sensitive group structures, critical clustered patterns, or collective behaviors, raising concerns about sensitive group-level privacy. In social and critical infrastructure networks, unauthorized community inference can reveal coordinated asset groups, operational hierarchies, and system dependencies that may be exploited for reconnaissance or profiling. We study a defensive setting in which a network (or defender) operator seeks to conceal a community of interest while making only small, utility-preserving modifications to the network. Our analysis shows that community concealment depends on two measurable factors: the connectivity at the community boundary and the feature similarity between the protected community and its neighbors. Guided by these observations, we introduce Feature-Community-guided DICE (FCom-DICE), a perturbation strategy built on DICE (Disconnect Internally Connect Externally) that rewires a set of structurally influential edges and adjusts node features to reduce the distinctiveness exploited by GNN message passing. Across synthetic benchmarks and real network graphs such as Facebook, Wikipedia, and Bitcoin Transactions, FCom-DICE consistently outperforms structure-only DICE under the same perturbation budgets. The largest improvements are observed for communities that are weakly connected to the rest of the network and well separated in feature space. These gains are achieved while preserving key structural and feature characteristics of the original network. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of feature-aware perturbations for reducing the recoverability of targeted communities under GNN-based community inference.

title: SCOPE: Selective Conformal Optimized Pairwise LLM Judging
comments: Accepted at ICML 2026. 23 pages (9 main plus appendix), 7 figures, 11 tables
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as scalable judges in pairwise evaluation, but they remain prone to miscalibration and biases. We propose \textsc{Scope} (Selective Conformal Optimized Pairwise Evaluation), a framework that calibrates an acceptance threshold so that, under exchangeability, the error rate among non-abstained judgments is at most a user-specified level $α$. To supply \textsc{Scope} with a bias-neutral uncertainty signal, we introduce Bidirectional Preference Entropy (BPE), which queries the judge under both response positions and converts the order-averaged preference probability into an entropy-based score. Across various pairwise judging benchmarks, BPE outperforms standard confidence proxies in calibration and discrimination, while \textsc{Scope} consistently satisfies the target risk bound (empirical FDR $\approx 0.097$--$0.099$ at $α=0.10$) and retains substantial coverage. Compared to vanilla baselines, \textsc{Scope} accepts up to $2.4\times$ more judgments under the same risk constraint, demonstrating that BPE enables reliable and high-coverage LLM-based evaluation.
